paras: The killing of an unnamed Black man at Taliulah, Louisiana, took place on the night of Saturday, 29 October 1881, the same day he was reported to have killed another Black man with a railway spike driver. The only known report, a one-sentence item in the Richland Beacon of Rayville, attributed his death, with a hedge, to a mob.

According to the Richland Beacon, "One negro killed another with a railway spike driver at Taliulah last Saturday," a date that falls on 29 October 1881 counting back from the paper's 5 November issue. The man accused of that killing "was himself killed that night, it is supposed, by a mob." The item gave neither man's name and did not say how, or exactly where, the second man was killed.
No report of an inquest, arrests or any official response appears in the coverage.

The Richland Beacon ran the news on 5 November 1881 as a bare line among short notes, with no headline, names or comment. Its wording stated the first killing as fact while presenting the mob's role only as something "supposed," and it identified both men solely as "negro." It was the sole published account of the episode located, and no later item gave names or followed up on the supposed mob.

bases: The only report says the accused man was killed the night of the killing he was charged with, 'it is supposed, by a mob' (A1).

A1 reports the man was killed the same night he killed another man and attributes the killing, tentatively ('it is supposed'), to a mob; it gives no size, no names and no stated motive, so the group, its illegality and its pretext rest on that one supposition (A1).
A single one-sentence brief in the Richland Beacon is the only report found (A1).
